title: Sweet Potato Pie
pitTemp: 400°F to roast the potatoes, 350°F to bake the pie
finish: Custard set, nutmeg on the nose, no pumpkin-spice impersonation
summary: Roasted sweet potato, evaporated milk, nutmeg. The Carolina pie that pumpkin tries to fake every November.
story: Sweet potato pie is not pumpkin pie in a different sweater. Roast the potatoes so they caramelize. Mash smooth. Evaporated milk, brown sugar, nutmeg, a little cinnamon, vanilla, eggs. It should taste like a root that worked for a living, not a candle. Church tables from the Carolinas to Kentucky put this next to the ham. It belongs next to whole hog too.

items: 1 unbaked 9-inch pie crust (same as the pecan pie, or store-bought without shame)

steps.title: Roast, don't boil
steps.body: Prick potatoes. 400°F 45–60 minutes until collapsed. Cool, peel, mash 2 cups packed. Boiling them waters the pie down. Don't.

steps.title: Custard
steps.body: Beat mash with brown sugar, milk, eggs, butter, vanilla, nutmeg, cinnamon, salt until smooth. A few fibers are honest. Lumps the size of marbles are not.

steps.title: Bake
steps.body: Pour into the crust. 350°F 45–55 minutes until the center barely jiggles. Cool completely. Whipped cream. A little extra nutmeg on top if you like people talking.

proTips.text: If it tastes like pumpkin pie you used too much cinnamon and not enough nutmeg. Nutmeg is the point.

milestones.label: Potatoes collapsed
milestones.hint: Roast, peel, mash 2 cups.

milestones.label: Smooth custard
milestones.hint: Nutmeg first. Cinnamon in the background.

milestones.label: Barely jiggles
milestones.hint: Cool all the way. Cream on the slice.

title: Hummingbird Cake
finish: Layers spring back, frosting set, pineapple still tasting like pineapple
summary: Banana, pineapple, pecan, cream-cheese frosting. The Alabama layer cake that showed up at every reunion and refused to leave.
story: Southern Living printed a hummingbird cake in 1978 and the South has not recovered. Banana and crushed pineapple keep it wet. Pecans in the batter and on the frosting. Cream cheese, not a sugar crust. It is a lot of cake. That is the assignment after a whole hog. Make the layers a day ahead; frost the morning of.

items: ½ cup chopped pecans for the sides

steps.title: Batter
steps.body: Heat oven 350°F. Grease and flour three 9-inch pans. Whisk flour, sugar, soda, cinnamon, salt. Stir in eggs and oil just to wet. Fold banana, pineapple with juice, pecans, vanilla. Divide.

steps.title: Bake
steps.body: 25–30 minutes until a toothpick is clean. Cool 10 minutes in pans, then racks. Completely cool before frosting or you have soup.

steps.title: Frost
steps.body: Beat cream cheese and butter. Powdered sugar, vanilla. Stack, frost, pecans on the sides. Fridge an hour if the kitchen is hot. Serve at cool room temp so the frosting isn't a brick.

proTips.text: Undrained pineapple. Drain it and you baked a dry banana cake with ambitions.

milestones.label: Batter folded
milestones.hint: Banana, pineapple with juice, pecans.

milestones.label: Layers cool
milestones.hint: Toothpick clean. Wait before frosting.

milestones.label: Frosted
milestones.hint: Cream cheese. Pecans on the sides.

title: Bourbon Bread Pudding
finish: Puffed, set in the center, sauce hot
summary: Stale bread, custard, raisins, a bourbon sauce you pour at the table. New Orleans close to a smoked-turkey night.
story: Bread pudding is what a bakery does with yesterday and a pit dinner does with extra. Stale French bread, a rich custard, raisins if you like them, pecans if you don't. The sauce is butter, brown sugar, cream, and enough bourbon that people notice. Don't drown the pan — sauce the plate. This is the Louisiana answer when pecan pie feels too Texan.

items: 1 lb stale French bread, torn in chunks
¾ cup raisins or chopped pecans

steps.title: Soak
steps.body: Bread in a buttered 9×13. Whisk milk, eggs, sugar, butter, vanilla, cinnamon, nutmeg, salt. Pour. Press the bread under. Raisins. Rest 20 minutes so it drinks.

steps.title: Bake
steps.body: 350°F 45–55 minutes until puffed and the center is set. A little jiggle at the very middle is fine. Rest 10 minutes.

steps.title: Sauce
steps.body: Melt butter, brown sugar, cream, salt. Simmer 2 minutes. Off heat, bourbon. Spoon over squares at the table. Keep extra in a little pitcher — someone will ask.

proTips.text: Stale bread. Fresh bread makes mush. If all you have is fresh, dry the chunks in a 300°F oven 15 minutes.

milestones.label: Bread soaked
milestones.hint: 20 minutes under custard.

milestones.label: Center set
milestones.hint: Puffed. Rest 10.

milestones.label: Bourbon sauce
milestones.hint: Off heat for the whiskey. Pour on the plate.

title: Blackberry Cobbler
finish: Purple juice bubbling through a golden lid
summary: Wild-dark berries, lemon, a sugar-dusted biscuit top. The Kentucky cobbler that stains the spoon and the napkin.
story: Blackberry cobbler is what you make when the fencerow is hanging heavy and the pit is already lit. Frozen berries work. Fresh wild ones work better. A little lemon and sugar, not a jar of jam. The lid is drop biscuits so the juice can breathe. Serve it warm. Vanilla ice cream will turn purple. That's how you know you did it.

items: 6 cups blackberries, fresh or frozen (don't thaw)

steps.title: Toss the berries
steps.body: Berries, sugar, cornstarch, lemon juice, zest, salt in a 2-quart baking dish or 10-inch skillet. If they're frozen, add another teaspoon of cornstarch.

steps.title: Lid
steps.body: Flour, sugar, baking powder, salt. Cut in butter. Buttermilk until shaggy. Drop on the fruit. Extra tablespoon of sugar on top.

steps.title: Bake
steps.body: 375°F 35–45 minutes until the top is brown and the purple is bubbling through. Rest 15 minutes. Ice cream. Don't wear a white shirt.

proTips.text: If you sweeten it like pie filling you hid the berry. Taste a raw one. Sugar should lift it, not bury it.

milestones.label: Berries tossed
milestones.hint: Sugar, starch, lemon.

milestones.label: Biscuit lid
milestones.hint: Dropped. Sugar dust.

milestones.label: Purple bubbling
milestones.hint: Rest 15. Ice cream.

title: Chess Pie
finish: Crackled sugar top, custard that slices, not weeps
summary: Butter, sugar, cornmeal, a little vinegar. The old Southern pie that tastes like a vanilla custard learned to stand up.
story: Chess pie is what you bake when the fruit is gone and the cupboard isn't. Eggs, sugar, butter, a spoon of cornmeal for grit, vinegar or lemon so it isn't candy. The top crackles. The inside is a set custard. Kentucky and the deeper South have been arguing about buttermilk vs. not for a century. This one uses a splash of vinegar and cornmeal — the older road. Serve small slices. It is richer than it looks.

items: 1 Tbsp white vinegar or lemon juice

steps.title: Whisk
steps.body: Sugar into melted butter. Eggs one at a time. Cornmeal, flour, vinegar, vanilla, milk, salt. It looks thin. That's correct.

steps.title: Bake
steps.body: Pour into the crust. 350°F 45–55 minutes until the top is golden and crackled and the center is just set. Tent the crust edge if it darkens.

steps.title: Cool
steps.body: Cool completely or it will slump. Room temp or cold from the fridge. No sauce. Maybe unsweetened whipped cream if the pit meal was already sweet.

proTips.text: The cornmeal is not optional decoration. Without it you made a sugar pie that weeps. The grit is the name.

milestones.label: Filling thin
milestones.hint: Butter, sugar, eggs, cornmeal, vinegar.

milestones.label: Top crackled
milestones.hint: Center just set. Tent the crust if needed.

milestones.label: Fully cool
milestones.hint: Slice small. It is richer than it looks.

title: Texas Sheet Cake
finish: Icing set to fudge, pecans stuck, still a little warm
summary: Thin chocolate cake, poured cocoa icing, pecans. The Texas potluck pan that feeds a whole pit crew.
story: Sheet cake is what you bake when there are too many people and not enough pie plates. Cocoa in the batter, buttermilk, a boiled icing you pour on the hot cake so it fuses. Pecans while the icing is wet. It should be fudgy, not a layer cake pretending. Serve in squares from the pan. Nobody needs a plate unless they ask.

steps.title: Batter
steps.body: Heat oven 350°F. Grease an 18×13 sheet pan (or 9×13 for a thicker cake). Whisk flour, sugar, soda, salt. Melt butter with cocoa and water. Pour over the dry, then buttermilk, eggs, vanilla. Spread.

steps.title: Bake
steps.body: 18×13: 18–22 minutes. 9×13: 28–32. Toothpick clean. Keep it in the pan.

steps.title: Pour the icing
steps.body: While it bakes, melt butter, cocoa, milk. Off heat, powdered sugar, vanilla. Pour over the hot cake. Pecans immediately. Cool until the icing sets. Cut squares.

proTips.text: Icing on a cold cake sits on top like frosting. Icing on a hot cake becomes the crust. Hot is the whole trick.

milestones.label: Cake done
milestones.hint: Toothpick clean. Leave it in the pan.

milestones.label: Icing poured hot
milestones.hint: Pecans now. Cool to fudge.

title: Peanut Butter Texas Sheet Cake
finish: Icing set to fudge, peanuts stuck, still a little warm
summary: Buttermilk sheet cake, boiled peanut butter icing poured on hot. The Texas chocolate sheet cake's cousin that shows up at the same potluck.
story: Same pan, same rush, no cocoa. You melt butter with water and peanut butter, pour it over flour and sugar, hit it with buttermilk and eggs. The icing is the same trick as the chocolate version: peanut butter, butter, milk, powdered sugar, poured on the hot cake so it fuses into a crust. Chopped peanuts while it's wet. It should taste like a peanut butter cup that learned manners. Feeds a crew. Travels in the pan.

steps.title: Batter
steps.body: Heat oven 350°F. Grease an 18×13 sheet pan (or 9×13 for thicker). Whisk flour, sugar, soda, salt. Melt butter with water and peanut butter until smooth. Pour over the dry, then buttermilk, eggs, vanilla. Spread.

steps.title: Bake
steps.body: 18×13: 18–22 minutes. 9×13: 28–32. Toothpick clean. Keep it in the pan.

steps.title: Pour the icing
steps.body: While it bakes, melt butter, peanut butter, and milk until smooth. Off heat: powdered sugar, vanilla, salt. Pour over the hot cake. Chopped peanuts immediately. Cool until the icing sets to fudge. Cut squares.

proTips.text: Creamy peanut butter in the batter and the icing. Crunchy in the pot seizes and makes lumps. Chopped peanuts on top are the crunch — that's the order.

milestones.label: Cake done
milestones.hint: Toothpick clean. Leave it in the pan.

milestones.label: Peanut butter icing hot
milestones.hint: Pour now. Peanuts on top. Cool to fudge.

title: Mimi's Chocolate Cobbler
finish: Crackly cake on top, hot fudge sauce underneath, ice cream melting
summary: A thin chocolate batter, a dry cocoa-sugar lid, boiling water poured over — don't stir. Mimi's pan: cake on top, pudding sauce below.
story: Every Southern Mimi has a chocolate cobbler that looks wrong until it isn't. You spread a humble cocoa batter in a pan, shower it with more sugar and cocoa, then pour a cup of boiling water over the whole mess and shove it in the oven without stirring. It bakes into a crust on top and a hot fudge lagoon underneath. Spoon it into bowls with vanilla ice cream. This is the 45-minute closer when the pit is still going and pie feels like a project.

steps.title: Batter
steps.body: Heat oven 350°F. Butter an 8×8 or 9×9 pan. Whisk flour, sugar, cocoa, baking powder, salt. Stir in milk, melted butter, vanilla until just smooth. Spread in the pan — it will look thin. That's the batter, not the cobbler yet.

steps.title: Don't stir
steps.body: Mix brown sugar, sugar, and cocoa. Sprinkle evenly over the batter. Pour the boiling water over the top. Do not stir. It looks like a mistake. It isn't.

steps.title: Bake and wait
steps.body: 350°F 35–40 minutes until the top is crackly and set and you can see sauce bubbling at the edge. Rest 10 minutes so the fudge thickens. Spoon into bowls — cake, then sauce. Ice cream is not optional.

proTips.text: If you stir after the water goes in you made chocolate soup. Pour, walk away, trust the oven. The sauce hides under the cake. That's the whole magic.

milestones.label: Batter spread
milestones.hint: Thin in the pan. Don't panic.

milestones.label: Water poured
milestones.hint: Sugar-cocoa lid, boiling water. Do not stir.

milestones.label: Sauce bubbling
milestones.hint: Crackly top. Rest 10. Ice cream.

title: Cola Cake
finish: Moist crumb, fudgy icing, cola in the background not a soda fountain
summary: Cocoa, buttermilk, a can of cola in the batter and the icing. The Deep South chocolate cake that showed up at every reunion.
story: Cola cake is sheet cake's cousin that went to Atlanta. The soda tenderizes the crumb and leaves a caramel note, not a fountain-drink taste. Marshmallows in the batter are a church-lady option. Pecans on the icing are not optional in my kitchen. Bake it in a 9×13. It travels.

steps.title: Batter
steps.body: 350°F. Grease a 9×13. Whisk flour, sugar, soda, salt. Melt butter with cocoa and cola. Combine, then buttermilk, eggs, vanilla. Fold marshmallows if using. Spread.

steps.title: Bake
steps.body: 30–35 minutes until a toothpick is clean. Marshmallows will melt into wet pockets. That's correct.

steps.title: Icing
steps.body: Melt butter, cocoa, cola. Off heat, powdered sugar, vanilla. Pour on the hot cake. Pecans. Cool in the pan.

proTips.text: Diet cola will not do this. The sugar in the soda is part of the chemistry. Drink the rest of the can. You've earned it.

milestones.label: Cake baked
milestones.hint: Toothpick clean. Marshmallows melted in.

milestones.label: Hot icing
milestones.hint: Cola icing, pecans, cool in the pan.

title: Red Velvet Cake
finish: Fine red crumb, tang from buttermilk, cream-cheese frosting
summary: Cocoa, buttermilk, vinegar, cream-cheese frosting. The Southern celebration cake that is not just a red vanilla.
story: Red velvet is a lightly cocoa cake with acid — buttermilk and vinegar — so the crumb is tender and the old recipes could blush with cocoa and food color. Cream cheese frosting, not ermine, unless your grandmother insists. Three layers. It is a birthday cake that also survives a pig pickin'.

steps.title: Batter
steps.body: 350°F. Grease three 8-inch pans. Whisk dry. Whisk oil, buttermilk, eggs, coloring, vinegar, vanilla. Combine just until smooth. Divide.

steps.title: Bake
steps.body: 25–30 minutes. Cool 10 in pans, then racks. Completely cool.

steps.title: Frost
steps.body: Beat cream cheese and butter. Powdered sugar, vanilla. Stack and frost. Fridge 30 minutes if the kitchen is hot. Serve cool, not ice-cold.

proTips.text: Cocoa is a teaspoon, not a chocolate cake. If it tastes like devil's food you used too much and lost the velvet.

milestones.label: Red batter
milestones.hint: Buttermilk, vinegar, a little cocoa.

milestones.label: Layers cool
milestones.hint: Don't frost warm.

milestones.label: Frosted
milestones.hint: Cream cheese. Cool room temp to serve.

title: Southern Pound Cake
finish: Crack down the center, tight crumb, crusty sugar edge
summary: Butter, sugar, eggs, flour. The old ratio cake that needs a glaze or a berry, not a lecture.
story: Pound cake used to be a pound of each. This one is a little kinder but still a butter cake with a crack down the top that means you did it right. Cream the butter and sugar longer than you think. Low oven. A bundt or a loaf. Serve with strawberries, peaches, or nothing but a plate. It is the cake you can make when the fruit cobbler already happened.

items: 1 cup heavy cream or whole milk

steps.title: Cream
steps.body: 325°F. Grease and flour a 10-cup bundt or two loaves. Beat butter and sugar 5–7 minutes until almost white. Eggs one at a time.

steps.title: Fold
steps.body: Whisk flour, baking powder, salt. Alternate with cream, starting and ending dry. Vanilla. Don't overmix once the flour is in.

steps.title: Bake
steps.body: Bundt 70–85 minutes, loaves 55–70, until a long skewer is clean. Cool 15 in the pan, then a rack. Overnight, wrapped, it slices cleaner.

proTips.text: Room-temp butter and eggs. Cold eggs in creamed butter make a curdled batter and a sad crumb.

milestones.label: Butter pale
milestones.hint: 5–7 minutes. Eggs one at a time.

milestones.label: Skewer clean
milestones.hint: Crack on top is honest. Cool in the pan 15.

title: Lemon Icebox Pie
pitTemp: None, or 350°F 15 minutes if you bake the crust
summary: Condensed milk, lemon, graham crust. The Gulf closer you make in the morning and forget until the meat is gone.
story: Icebox pie is what the South does when the oven is already full of a hog. Sweetened condensed milk, lemon juice, yolks — it sets in the fridge like a magic trick. Graham crust. Meringue if you want to show off, whipped cream if you want to eat. It should make your mouth pucker, then the sugar catches up.

steps.title: Crust
steps.body: Mix crumbs, sugar, butter. Press into a 9-inch pie plate. Bake 350°F 8–10 minutes (or skip the oven and chill 15). Cool.

steps.title: Fill
steps.body: Whisk condensed milk, lemon juice, zest, yolks, salt until it thickens a little. Pour. It will look loose. The fridge does the rest.

steps.title: Icebox
steps.body: Fridge at least 4 hours, overnight better. Whipped cream or a torch-toasted meringue. Keep cold. It weeps in a hot kitchen.

proTips.text: Bottled lemon juice tastes like a cleaning product. Squeeze the fruit. The zest is half the perfume.

milestones.label: Crust in
milestones.hint: Press hard. Bake or chill.

milestones.label: Filled
milestones.hint: Condensed milk, real lemon, yolks.

milestones.label: Icebox set
milestones.hint: Four hours minimum. Cream on top.
